metadata.description: Structured knowledge base of evidence-backed land, soil, water and biodiversity interventions. Each record encodes applicability conditions, causal mechanism, quantified impact ranges, source attribution, and confidence — designed to be retrieved (via src/knowledge_retriever.py) rather than hard-coded into prompts.
metadata.note_on_sources: Figures are drawn from widely-cited ranges published by FAO, IPCC, CBD and peer-reviewed meta-analyses (e.g. Rodale Institute, Project Drawdown). Ranges are directional/illustrative rather than site-specific measurements. Before production use, verify each figure against the primary study, since real-world outcomes vary strongly by soil type, climate and baseline degradation.

interventions.title: Legume-based cover cropping
interventions.mechanism: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen via rhizobia symbiosis and add root biomass and residue between cash-crop cycles, feeding soil microbial communities and increasing aggregate stability.
interventions.source: FAO Soils Portal — Soil Organic Carbon guidance; FAO 'Conservation Agriculture' technical briefs

interventions.title: Agroforestry / intercropping (tree-crop integration)
interventions.mechanism: Woody perennials add deep-rooted carbon inputs and leaf litter, buffer topsoil microclimate (reduced evapotranspiration and wind erosion), and create vertical habitat structure that supports insects, birds and soil fauna absent in monocultures.

quantified_impact.change: canopy cooling of 1-3°C at soil surface

interventions.source: FAO Agroforestry Working Papers; IPCC AR6 WG2 (agricultural adaptation chapter)

interventions.title: Native riparian buffer strips
interventions.mechanism: Vegetated strips along waterways filter nutrient and sediment runoff before it reaches water bodies, and provide continuous habitat corridors that counteract fragmentation caused by adjacent farmland.
interventions.source: USDA NRCS riparian buffer studies; CBD guidance on freshwater ecosystem connectivity

interventions.title: No-till / reduced tillage
interventions.mechanism: Avoiding mechanical soil inversion preserves fungal hyphal networks and soil aggregate structure, slowing organic carbon oxidation and reducing erosion-driven topsoil loss.
interventions.source: FAO Conservation Agriculture program data; IPCC AR6 WG3 agricultural mitigation chapter

interventions.title: Diversified crop rotation (beyond 2-crop cycles)
interventions.mechanism: Rotating functionally different crops (e.g. cereal-legume-brassica) disrupts pest and pathogen life cycles, diversifies root exudate chemistry, and reduces reliance on synthetic inputs.
interventions.source: FAO 'Save and Grow' sustainable intensification report

interventions.title: Hedgerows and field-margin restoration
interventions.mechanism: Woody and flowering field margins provide nesting habitat and forage for pollinators and natural pest predators, and act as stepping-stone habitat that reduces functional fragmentation between larger habitat patches.
interventions.source: CBD Agricultural Biodiversity technical briefs; European Commission farmland biodiversity studies

interventions.title: Rotational (managed) grazing
interventions.mechanism: Time-controlled rotation between paddocks prevents overgrazing of any single area, allowing root systems to recover between grazing events, which increases root carbon deposition and grass species diversity.
interventions.source: FAO grassland management guidance; Project Drawdown 'Managed Grazing' analysis

interventions.title: Wetland restoration / rehydration
interventions.mechanism: Restoring hydrology in drained wetlands re-establishes anaerobic soil conditions that store carbon, filters pollutants, and recreates specialized habitat that supports disproportionately high biodiversity relative to area.

quantified_impact.change: high per-hectare sequestration versus degraded state
substantial increase, especially waterfowl and amphibians

interventions.source: IPCC Wetlands Supplement (2013); CBD wetland ecosystem guidance

interventions.title: Mixed-species native reforestation (vs. monoculture plantation)
interventions.mechanism: Multiple native species create structurally and functionally diverse canopy layers, supporting a wider range of niches than single-species plantations, and are more resilient to pest outbreaks and climate stress.

quantified_impact.change: markedly higher than monoculture plantations of equal age
reduced when planted as corridors between existing patches

interventions.source: IPBES Global Assessment (2019); FAO Forest Landscape Restoration guidance

interventions.title: Biochar soil amendment
interventions.mechanism: Pyrolyzed organic matter is chemically stable in soil for centuries, directly raising measured soil carbon while its porous structure improves water-holding capacity and provides microhabitat for beneficial microbes.

quantified_impact.change: durable increase, magnitude depends on application rate

interventions.source: IPCC AR6 WG3 (carbon dioxide removal chapter); IBI (International Biochar Initiative) technical guidance

interventions.title: Integrated pest management (IPM) / reduced pesticide reliance
interventions.mechanism: Substituting broad-spectrum pesticide applications with biological controls, monitoring thresholds and targeted intervention reduces non-target mortality of pollinators, soil fauna and natural predators.

quantified_impact.change: measurable recovery within 1-2 seasons of reduced broad-spectrum use

interventions.source: FAO IPM guidance; IPBES Pollinators Assessment (2016)

interventions.title: Rainwater harvesting / check dams (semi-arid water management)
interventions.mechanism: Small-scale water-harvesting structures slow surface runoff, increase groundwater recharge and extend soil moisture availability into dry periods, which is frequently the limiting factor for both crop and native vegetation survival in semi-arid systems.
interventions.source: FAO water-harvesting technical manuals; IPCC AR6 WG2 (water security chapter)

interventions.title: Organic mulching
interventions.mechanism: A surface layer of organic residue reduces soil evaporation, buffers surface temperature extremes, and gradually decomposes to add organic matter.

interventions.title: Silvopasture (integrating trees into grazing land)
interventions.mechanism: Combining trees with livestock grazing adds a vertical habitat layer, provides shade that reduces heat stress on livestock and understory vegetation, and adds deep root carbon inputs absent from open pasture.

quantified_impact.change: increase vs open pasture, especially birds and insects
increase from tree root and litter inputs

interventions.source: FAO Agroforestry Working Papers; Project Drawdown 'Silvopasture' analysis

interventions.title: Habitat corridors to reduce fragmentation
interventions.mechanism: Connecting isolated habitat patches with vegetated corridors allows gene flow, seasonal migration and recolonization after local extinction events, directly counteracting the population-isolation effects of fragmentation.

quantified_impact.change: improved via increased gene flow between patches
reduced local extinction risk in small patches

interventions.source: IPBES Global Assessment (2019); landscape ecology meta-analyses on corridor efficacy
